newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to consolidate, aluminium shaky.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to consolidate, aluminium shaky.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Technically overbought copper runs the risk of a downside correction, but buoyant indicators suggest a consolidation period above $2,500 may be more likely, analysts said.
Aluminium remains under pressure and could test the low end of its recent trading range, they added.
COPPER - Persistant speculative buying catapulted copper to fresh one-year highs last week and lent a decidedly bullish tone to the market.
But the uptrend sooner or later will have to be tempered by copper's overbought status, with the 14-day RSI above the key 70 level for two weeks running, analysts said.

"After failing to break convincingly above resistance at $2,545, the market may try the downside next week. Nearby support is seen at $2,520, which relates to a key level on the Comex market and then at $2,500," brokers Brandeis said in a commentary.
But other analysts noted that uptrending 10- and 30-day moving averages would at least keep the market in consolidation mode for the time being.
At 0745 GMT three months copper was trading at $2,520/$2,523, compared to $2,529 at Friday's kerb close.
ALUMINIUM - The market is displaying markedly less ebulliance than flagship copper and a test of the $1,610 and possibly $1,600 support levels could be in store, analysts said.
Short term moving averages are heading lower, while the 14-day RSI is neutral.

"Chartwise the market appears to be running out of steam on the upside, closing well below support from the 30-day moving average at $1,630. A test of the bottom end of the range looks likely," Brandeis said.
At 0745 GMT three months aluminium was indicated at $1,611/$1,613, versus $1,619 at Friday's kerb close.
